title: Rules of Warfare

questions.question: What should Israel not fear when going to battle?
options: Horses, chariots, and people more numerous than them
questions.correctAnswer: Horses, chariots, and people more numerous than them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:1 (ESV): "When you go out to war... and see horses and chariots and a people more numerous than you, you shall not be afraid..."

questions.question: Who speaks to the people before battle to encourage them?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:2 (ESV): "...the priest shall come forward and speak to the people..."

questions.question: Who is excused from battle because he built a new house?
options: The man who has not dedicated it
questions.correctAnswer: The man who has not dedicated it
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:5 (ESV): "Is there any man that has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go back..."

questions.question: Who is excused because he planted a vineyard?
options: The man who has not enjoyed its fruit
questions.correctAnswer: The man who has not enjoyed its fruit
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:6 (ESV): "And is there any man who has planted a vineyard and has not enjoyed its fruit? Let him go back..."

questions.question: Who is excused because he is betrothed?
options: The man who has not taken her to be his wife
questions.correctAnswer: The man who has not taken her to be his wife
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:7 (ESV): "And is there any man who has betrothed a wife and has not taken her? Let him go back..."

questions.question: Who else is excused from battle to prevent disheartening others?
options: The man who is fearful and fainthearted
questions.correctAnswer: The man who is fearful and fainthearted
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:8 (ESV): "Is there any man who is fearful and fainthearted? Let him go back..."

questions.question: What must be offered to a city before attacking it?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:10 (ESV): "When you draw near to a city to fight against it, offer terms of peace to it."

questions.question: If a city accepts peace, what happens to the people?
options: They shall become forced labor and serve you
questions.correctAnswer: They shall become forced labor and serve you
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:11 (ESV): "...all the people found in it shall do forced labor for you and shall serve you."

questions.question: If a city refuses peace, what happens to the males?
options: Put every male to the sword
questions.correctAnswer: Put every male to the sword
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:13 (ESV): "then... you shall put all its males to the sword."

questions.question: Which cities must have everything that breathes destroyed?
options: Cities of the nations given as an inheritance (Canaanites, etc.)
questions.correctAnswer: Cities of the nations given as an inheritance (Canaanites, etc.)
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:16 (ESV): "But in the cities of these peoples... you shall save alive nothing that breathes..."

questions.question: Why must they utterly destroy the Hittites, Amorites, etc.?
options: That they may not teach you to do according to all their abominable practices
questions.correctAnswer: That they may not teach you to do according to all their abominable practices
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:18 (ESV): "that they may not teach you to do according to all their abominable practices..."

questions.question: What trees may NOT be cut down during a siege?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:19 (ESV): "...you shall not destroy its trees by wielding an ax against them, for you may eat from them..."

questions.question: What trees MAY be cut down?
options: Only trees that you know are not trees for food
questions.correctAnswer: Only trees that you know are not trees for food
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:20 (ESV): "Only the trees that you know are not trees for food you may destroy and cut down..."

questions.question: What is the rhetorical question asked about the tree of the field?
options: "Is the tree of the field a man that it should be besieged by you?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Is the tree of the field a man that it should be besieged by you?"
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:19 (ESV): "...Are the trees in the field human, that they should be besieged by you?"

questions.question: How does the priest address the army?
options: "Hear, O Israel, today you are drawing near for battle against your enemies..."
questions.correctAnswer: "Hear, O Israel, today you are drawing near for battle against your enemies..."
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 20:3 (ESV): "and shall say to them, 'Hear, O Israel, today you are drawing near for battle...'"

key_verse_text: When you go out to war against your enemies, and see horses and chariots and people more numerous than you, you shall not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God is with you, who brought you up from the land of Egypt. (ESV)
